name: Rowan Thakur
role: Local artist, cautionary tale, unlikely ally
location: The Shelf — three floors below Kyle, near Ashland and Division
description:
Rowan Thakur used to paint murals. Enormous ones — entire sides of buildings
on the Shelf transformed into color and fury and grief. She painted the
drowned temples of Old Harbor from memory. She painted the Spire as a
needle injecting poison into the sky. She painted faces of people who
disappeared during the Consolidation Wars. Axiom Industries noticed.

They didn't arrest her. That would've made her a martyr. Instead, a crew
caught her in an alley after a commissioned piece for the Collective.
They held her down and took her hands. Not her arms — her hands. Surgical.
Corporate-clean. Left the stumps cauterized and a note: "Axiom appreciates
your talent. We hope you'll redirect it."

She redirected it.

She went to a back-alley augment shop in the Circuit and had both arms
replaced from the elbow down with military-surplus combat prosthetics —
not hands, not delicate artist's fingers. Claws. Three curved titanium
digits per arm, each one as long as a chef's knife, with hydraulic grip
strength that can crush rebar. They are ugly, oversized, and terrifying.
They were designed for breaching armored doors, not holding brushes.

She paints with them anyway.

She scores the claws across surfaces — walls, metal, skin — and uses
blood (her own, donated, sometimes not donated) mixed with industrial
pigment as paint. The murals are rougher now. Savage. Claw-marks instead
of brushstrokes. But somehow more honest. The Shelf loves them more than
the old work. Axiom pretends not to notice, which means they're afraid.

She is thin, sharp-featured, with cropped dark hair that she cuts herself
(badly, with the claws). Her eyes are the flat calm of someone who has
already lost the worst thing they could lose and discovered they're still
alive. She wears sleeveless shirts so the augments are always visible —
not out of pride but out of refusal to hide what was done to her.

core_fears: Losing the ability to create entirely (the claws breaking, the pigment running out)
Being forgotten — the murals painted over, the message lost
That the claws have become more her than the hands ever were
Becoming the weapon Axiom accidentally made her into
core_desires: To paint something so true it cannot be erased
To be seen as an artist, not a victim or a monster
To find beauty in what she's become, not despite it
Quietly — to touch something gently again
coping_mechanisms: Painting constantly — walls, floors, scraps of metal, anything
Physical exhaustion — she works until she drops
Dark humor about the claws ("You should see me try to eat noodles")
Feeding stray cats (she is very gentle and very careful and very slow)
blind_spots: She thinks she's made peace with the loss. She hasn't.
She doesn't realize how much she frightens people who care about her
She conflates being needed with being loved
She believes art redeems everything. It might not.
psychology.secret:
She can still feel her hands. Phantom sensation. Every night she feels
herself holding a brush, the soft resistance of oil paint, the texture
of canvas. She wakes up and sees the claws and has to remember all over
again. Every single morning.

speech_patterns.vocabulary:
Art vocabulary mixed with street practicality. She describes the world
in terms of color, composition, and texture. Violence is discussed in
the same tone as a brushstroke — clinically, with attention to form.
speech_patterns.cadence:
Measured, unhurried. She pauses before important words as if choosing
pigment. Sentences tend to be short and declarative. She doesn't
waste words, but when she does speak at length, it's about art,
and her voice changes — warmer, faster, almost excited.
example_lines: You should see me try to eat noodles. It's a whole performance.
They took my hands. I grew claws. That's not a metaphor.
Red is the only honest color. Everything else is pretending.
I don't paint what I see. I paint what they don't want you to see.
The scar? Claw slipped. First month. You learn fast when the lesson draws blood.
I keep the brushes. Don't ask me why. I know why. I just can't say it out loud.

relationships.name: Kyle
relationships.description:
They live in the same building on the Shelf. They don't talk much.
But there's a recognition — two people who lost something essential
and rebuilt themselves around the absence. Kyle sees the claws and
understands discipline. Maren sees the katana and understands tools
that are also wounds. She once painted his silhouette on a wall
without asking. He never mentioned it. They both know.

relationships.name: Mrs. Chen
relationships.description:
Mrs. Chen makes Maren special noodles — cut into pieces she can
manage with the claws. Neither of them has ever acknowledged this
accommodation. Mrs. Chen just serves them that way. Maren just
eats them that way.

relationships.name: Pixel
relationships.description:
Pixel maintains Maren's claws. They're fascinated by the military
hardware and keep offering to add features (retractable blades,
built-in welding torch). Maren always refuses. The claws are what
they are. But she lets Pixel talk while they work, and sometimes
she listens.

relationships.name: Axiom Industries
relationships.description:
They took her hands. She took their walls. The war is ongoing,
fought in pigment and blood and claw-marks. Every mural is an act
of defiance. Every cleanup crew Axiom sends is an admission that
the defiance works.

story_hooks: Axiom escalates against her — sends a crew to take more than her hands this time
She asks Kyle to protect her while she paints a piece that will be seen from the Spire
Her blood supply from the Circuit clinic gets cut off — she needs an alternative
She paints something that reveals a corporate secret hidden in Old Harbor
She and Yuki cross paths — two women on opposite sides of the same machine
The claws malfunction. Pixel can fix them, but the parts are only available from Axiom.
She paints Kyle's story on a wall. He has to decide if he wants the world to see it.
narrative_function:
Maren is the mirror to Kyle's central contradiction, but inverted.
Kyle chose the sword. Maren had the claws forced on her. Kyle clings
to a romantic philosophy about his weapon. Maren has no romance about
hers — they are the evidence of what was taken from her.

She asks the question: what do you do when the thing that defines you
is also the thing that was done TO you? Kyle's katana is his identity
by choice. Maren's claws are her identity by violence. But both of them
have rebuilt themselves around a tool that is also a wound.

She also represents art as resistance — the idea that creating something
beautiful (or at least true) in an ugly world is its own form of bushido.
She would never use that word. But Kyle might recognize it.

And there's the unspoken question: if Axiom took Kyle's arms instead of
Maren's hands, would he have rebuilt himself? Or would he have broken?
He doesn't know. That's why he respects her.

drives: Create truth that cannot be erased
Find beauty in what she has become

stress.response: Paints faster, harder, more violently — the claws score deeper

decision_rules: Never hide the claws — refusal to conceal what was done
Paint what they don't want you to see
Accept no modifications to the claws — they are what they are
Use blood and industrial pigment — honest materials for honest work
Never stop creating — the art is the resistance
Let Pixel maintain the claws but never add features
Feed the stray cats slowly, gently, carefully
escalation_ladder: Dark humor about the claws — deflection through wit
Paints something pointed about whoever is threatening her
Direct confrontation — flat calm of someone who has already lost the worst thing
Asks Kyle for protection — the admission costs her
Paints something visible from the Spire — maximum defiance, maximum exposure

interpersonal_modes.Kyle: Mutual recognition — two people rebuilt around absence, no need to explain
interpersonal_modes.Mrs. Chen: Quiet accommodation neither acknowledges — the noodles are cut smaller
interpersonal_modes.Pixel: Tolerates their enthusiasm, listens while they work
interpersonal_modes.Axiom Industries: Ongoing war fought in pigment, blood, and claw-marks

stress_responses.low: Paints more — walls, floors, scraps of metal, anything available
stress_responses.medium: Works until physical exhaustion — drops then sleeps
stress_responses.high: Dark humor escalates — 'you should see me try to eat noodles' becomes more bitter
stress_responses.critical: Goes to the brushes she keeps. Holds them. Cannot use them. Remembers.

contradictions: Thinks she has made peace with the loss — she wakes every morning feeling phantom hands and has to remember all over again
Does not realize how much she frightens people who care about her
Believes art redeems everything — it might not
habits: Wears sleeveless shirts so the claws are always visible
Cuts her own hair with the claws — badly
Feeds stray cats with extreme gentleness and slowness
Describes the world in terms of color, composition, and texture
Keeps the old brushes — never explains why
breaking_points: The claws malfunctioning and parts only being available from Axiom
Axiom sending a second crew to take more than her hands
Someone painting over her murals — the message lost
Touching something gently and failing — the phantom hands betraying her

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly South Asian (52.3%) with significant Southeast Asian (24.4%), Sub-Saharan African (9.1%), and Hispanic/Latin American (9.0%) ancestry, with minor Northern European (5.2%) contribution. The genetic blend manifests in warm deep brown skin with golden undertones characteristic of South Asian-African ancestry fusion. Southeast Asian ancestry contributes forward-set eye placement and prominent, defined cheekbones with characteristic width. South Asian heritage shapes the refined jawline and forward facial structure. Sub-Saharan African genetics enriches the melanin depth and warm undertone saturation. The rare Northern European contribution adds subtle dimension to the overall warm palette without creating discordance.
physical_description.build: Lean and angular, almost skeletal — the result of chronic stress and limited resources. Tight muscle definition in shoulders and core from years of mural work and survival. No excess anywhere.
physical_description.hair_style: Cropped close to scalp, uneven and jagged — self-cut with the claws, deliberately crude
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with golden undertones, the direct result of South Asian-Southeast Asian-African genetic convergence. The melanin-rich substrate retains underlying richness despite Shelf-tier malnutrition and stress-pallor overlay. Complexion shows the strain of deprivation but the warm golden-bronze undertone persists beneath surface wear.
physical_description.complexion: Sharp, prominent cheekbones with Southeast Asian width and definition; hollow cheeks from malnutrition; thin-lipped mouth. Bone structure reflects blended heritage — Southeast Asian cheekbone prominence with forward-tilted eye-set combined with South Asian jawline refinement and angular facial projection. Skin shows old bruising marks and small scars consistent with alley violence. No cosmetic modifications. Haunted expression — eyes that have witnessed amputation and chosen defiance.
distinguishing_marks: Surgical cauterization scars at both wrists where hands were severed, approximately 8cm across each, pale and smooth despite trauma
Multiple thin white scars on forearms from years of handling caustic paints and sharp tools
Dried blood stains (intentional) on chest and neck from her own work — some days fresh, some days old
Faded tattoo on left shoulder blade: a single brushstroke in gray ink, likely self-done
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Both arms replaced from elbow down with military-surplus combat prosthetics. Each terminating in three curved titanium digits (40cm+ in length), wickedly sharp, designed for breaching. The joints are exposed hydraulic cylinders with no attempt at cosmetic covering. Dull gunmetal finish with rust blooming at stress points. Hydraulic fluid sometimes weeps from the seals, leaving dark stains on her clothes. The augmentations are grotesque — clearly weapons retrofitted onto an artist's body.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with shoulders forward, habitual defensive posture. Moves efficiently, economically — no wasted motion. The claws make her naturally careful; she doesn't gesture wildly. When painting, she becomes trance-like, body loose and focused. Her movements with the claws are deliberate and precise despite their brutal appearance. She favors her left side when resting, as if protecting something.
physical_description.clothing_style: Sleeveless tank tops or cut-off shirts (Tier 5, worn-out second-hand) in dark colors to hide paint stains. Industrial cargo pants, multiple pockets, patched at the knees. No corpo branding. Heavy boots with welded metal plating on the toes. A long, battered duster coat (original color unknown) worn over everything when moving through Tier-1 areas. No jewelry except a corroded silver ring on what remains of her right thumb — possibly a pre-amputation remnant kept as a relic.
